_desc: How to reach Zermatt by train from Zürich, Geneva and Lucerne: the change at Visp, journey times, the Gornergrat railway and the best time to visit the Matterhorn.
b1: How to Get to Zermatt by Train
b2: By WoW Train · Updated October 2026 · 4 min read
b3: A car-free village below the Matterhorn. There is no road you can drive into Zermatt, so the train is not an alternative: it is the way in. The last stretch, up the valley on the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn, is a scenic ride in its own right.
b4: What is the route to Zermatt?
b5: Take a train to Visp, then change to the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn to Zermatt. From Zürich the whole journey takes roughly 3h 30m–3h 45m; from Geneva roughly 3h 15m–3h 30m; from Lucerne about four hours via Bern. Trains from Visp to Zermatt run about every half hour, and the connections are timed, so a single change is usually painless.
b7: 1. Board a long-distance train toward Brig and get off at Visp.
b8: 2. Change to the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn on the platform provided; the connection is usually short.
b9: 3. Ride up the valley to Zermatt; the station is in the village centre.
b10: When is the best time to go?
b11: July to September is the main hiking season, with the best chance of clear Matterhorn views.
b12: December to April is the ski season; book trains and rooms early around holidays.
b13: Mornings are usually clearer; the mountain is often in cloud by afternoon.
b14: What to do once you are there?
b15: The Gornergrat railway — a cogwheel train of roughly 30–35 minutes to a viewpoint opposite the Matterhorn.
b16: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise — a cable car to one of the highest viewpoints in Europe.
b17: The Riffelsee — the lake where the Matterhorn reflects in the water, reached on foot from the Gornergrat line.
b18: The Glacier Express — leaves from Zermatt for St. Moritz, a famously slow and scenic ride of about eight hours.
b19: You have seen it. Now go. The key is the change at Visp: book your train there and the rest is up the valley. Every operator, one secure checkout.

b30: The tip worth knowing: most journeys involve one change at Visp, in the Rhône valley. From there the narrow-gauge train climbs to Zermatt in roughly 1h 10m–1h 20m. Cars have to stop at Täsch, so you do not need to bring one.
